😊 Hello! It's great to hear that you are interested in **Spring Boot**, a powerful Java framework for building web applications quickly and easily. Here’s how we can get started on your journey towards getting an internship with this skillset under your belt:

1. Understand the Basics of Spring Framework: Before diving into Spring Boot specifically, make sure you have a solid understanding of the foundational concepts in **Spring** framework such as dependency injection and aspect-oriented programming (AOP). These are essential for effectively working with any version of spring including boot.

2. Learn Key Concepts & Syntax: Familiarize yourself with Spring Boot's key components like `Application`, `@ConfigurationProperties` annotations, properties files, autoconfiguration etc., as well as the basic syntax and structure required to develop a simple **Spring Boot** application. 

3. Practice Building Simple Applications: Start by building small projects such as CRUD applications for various data sources which are commonly asked in interviews or used in real-world scenarios like eCommerce sites, social media platforms etc., using Spring Boot and embedded Tomcat server (or Jetty). This will help you understand the basics of web application development.

4. Learn about RESTful APIs: As most internships involve developing back-end services for various applications or websites - a common practice in many tech companies is to create **RESTful** (**Representational State Transfer**) based, easy and lightweight API endpoints using Spring Boot's features like `@RestController`, `ResponseEntity` etc.

5. Hands-on Project Ideas: Here are some project ideas with their associated resources for learning by doing (alongside understanding the theory): 
   - **Online Shopping Cart** – build a simple eCommerce cart application, which can be found in this [tutorial](https://www.javatpoint.com/spring-boot-project). 
   
   - **Restaurant Reservation System** – Learn how to create an interactive reservation system using Spring Boot and MySQL by following the project idea presented here: [Spring Boot CRUD Application with MySql Database](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/spring-boot-crud-application-with-mysql/).
   
   - **Weather Forecast App** – Learn to build a weather forecast application by following this comprehensive tutorial on Spring Boot [tutorialspoint](https://www.tutorialspoint.com/Spring5_RESTful_Web_Services/HelloWorldRestFullExample.htm). 
   
6. Build Project Portfolio: As you complete your projects, build a portfolio website to showcase them using **HTML** and **CSS** with Spring Boot as the backend framework for managing application data dynamically (like creating new records or deleting existing ones), which can be found in this [tutorial](https://www.baeldung.com/spring-boot-thymeleaf).

7. Learn about Job Market Requirements: Research common job market requirements and expectations for **Spring Boot** internships, such as the level of experience required (Junior or Senior), preferred programming languages to know alongside Spring Framework like JavaScript etc., which you can find in this [resource](https://www.springguides.com/articles).

8. Networking and Job Applications: Join industry networking groups, tech meetups for meeting professionals working with **Spring Boot** or related technologies to gain more insights into the job market as well learn about potential internship opportunities directly from individuals in your target companies (like Meetup links can be found here [meetup.com](https://www.meetup.com/search?q=spring+boot)). Don't forget to prepare a tailored resume and cover letter showcasing the projects you have worked on, along with any certifications or courses that may strengthen your profile (You can get templates for both from this (https://www.resumegenius.com/)).

9. Mock Interviews: Practice mock interviews to simulate a real interview experience and gain confidence in presenting yourself as an ideal candidate with strong **Spring Boot** skills using resources like Pramp or VirtualInterview (Links can be found here [Pramp](https://pramp.com/) & [VirtualInterview](https://www.virtualinterview.co/))

10. Prepare for Interviews: Study common interview questions, prepare answers with concrete examples from your projects and research company-specific expectations by preparing well before the actual interviews (You can find some tips here [SpringGuide](http://springguide.com/)). 

Remember to stay persistent in learning new features Take your time.
